target.title: fix(qa-lab): runtime parity stays bounded when mock debug snapshots are oversized
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QA runtime parity reports could stall or consume unbounded memory when a mock provider debug snapshot grows unexpectedly large.

## Why This Change Was Made

The QA-lab runtime parity mock `/debug/requests` capture now uses the existing plugin SDK bounded response reader with a 1 MiB cap. Overflow and malformed debug payloads keep the existing best-effort `null` result so transcript-derived tool-call fallback remains the recovery path.

## User Impact

QA runtime parity runs stay responsive when local mock debug payloads are oversized, while normal debug snapshots continue to contribute tool-call ordering details.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: oversized mock debug snapshots are bounded, cancel the stream, release the SSRF guard, and fall back to transcript-derived tool calls.
- Current-head proof at b3d8b742d9159ba0d7626e535f1f30928206b227: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.test.ts` passed with 8 tests.
- PR diff hygiene: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: the runtime parity loader returns `null` for an oversized mock debug snapshot, allowing the transcript fallback path to remain authoritative.
